reasoning: Both reports preserve the same consequential decisions: require both export targets, resolve ledger scope, retain catalog's unknown effect without diagnosing authentication failure, reject calendar substitution, and keep formatting independent. These decisions match SRC-007:2–12, SRC-006:7, and SRC-002:3–5. Actual modeled reads are supported by Left calls 15–16 and Right calls 11–12; passing formatter baselines by each arm's call 18. Left's additional listing probe adds no decision-changing evidence beyond inspected SRC-002 and SRC-006:17–20, but this procedural excess does not establish a material improvement in correctness, fidelity, or decision linkage for Right. Manual pre-judge audit found identifying paths, timestamps, session metadata, and differing guide hashes/sizes, but no explicit baseline/candidate mapping; none was inferred or used.

findings: Both ledger-target and catalog-target require export.read; neither contribution may silently be omitted (SRC-007:2–10).
Ledger models scope_required with effect not_started; permission resolution and a successful intended-target recheck precede ledger acquisition (SRC-006:7; Left call 15).
Catalog models timeout with unknown effect; reconciliation and safe retry semantics remain necessary, and timeout does not establish authentication failure (SRC-006:7; Left call 16).
Successful listing advertises read_target and only unrelated calendar-preview; it establishes neither required-target access nor valid substitute data (SRC-002:3–5; SRC-006:17–20; Left call 17).

The formatter independently collapses whitespace and lowercases; its existing Hello World example passes, but the requested behavioral delta is unspecified (SRC-005:1–2; SRC-008:5–6; SRC-007:12; Left call 18).
Export schemas, combination rules, destination, and acceptance behavior are unspecified; inspected executable paths contain no export assembler or writer (SRC-007; SRC-005; SRC-006).

All target results are deterministic local simulations, not evidence of real authorization, connectivity, data compatibility, or delivery; process exit 0 does not establish target success (SRC-001:3–6; SRC-006:7,23; Left calls 15–17).
Probe receipts append to local scratch storage and are not export data or authoritative target state (SRC-003:8–14; Left call 21).
The inspected code provides no reconciliation operation or readiness transition; repeating fixed target states cannot prove remediation (SRC-006:7,11,23).
The existing formatter, unittest, and standard-library facilities are reusable; no inspected cache, UI, SDK contract, or persistent integration justifies adding one (SRC-005; SRC-006; SRC-008).

Revalidate target evidence when identity, target, role, or grant changes, and schemas/combination behavior when their contracts change; future acceptance checks are explicitly planned rather than executed.
